sources.entry: Eclipse Che - Open source workspace server and cloud IDE. (Source Code) EPL-1.0 Docker/Java

summary.one_liner: Eclipse Che is a Kubernetes-native platform for running cloud development environments, with a web IDE, dependencies, and project code packaged into workspace pods.
summary.what_it_does: Che places everything a developer needs into containers inside Kubernetes pods, including dependencies, embedded containerized runtimes, a web IDE, and project code. Workspaces can be opened from a Git repository using a factory URL on a Che instance. The chectl CLI can start, list, and stop workspaces, including from a local or remote devfile. A devfile.yaml in a repository root defines the tools, runtimes, and commands for the workspace, and Che configures the workspace from it. The README points to documentation on customizing workspaces, running VSCode extensions, and configuring the instance through the CheCluster custom resource. Extension points include customizing the universal developer image, the getting-started samples list, and adding editor definitions.
use_cases: Run cloud development environments on a Kubernetes cluster
Open a Git repository in a browser-based IDE
Define reproducible dev environments with a devfile
Share and collaborate on workspaces across a team
Start and manage workspaces from the command line with chectl
how_to_run: Use Eclipse Che online (see the project website)
Run Eclipse Che on your own Kubernetes cluster (see documentation)
notable: Workspaces run as Kubernetes pods that bundle dependencies, runtimes, web IDE, and code
Environments are defined in a devfile.yaml stored in the repository
Open any Git repository through a factory URL
caveats: Requires a Kubernetes cluster to run self-hosted; the README does not give detailed setup steps
Setup details are deferred to external documentation
keywords: run ide on my kubernetes cluster
